title: Screening
tocPath: APPROACH TO PATIENTS WITH EMERGENCY CONDITIONS
Changing ART in Children Under 15 Years
Screening, Diagnosis and Management of Common Opportunistic Infections in RoC with AHD

blocks.text: Screening

From the age of 10 years, screen for renal disease (proteinuria by urine dipstick) and retinopathy annually Annual screening for risk of stroke by transcranial Doppler from the age of 2years to 16years.

blocks.text: Pharmacological Management
Supportive therapy
A: folic acid (PO) 5mg 24hourly
AND
A: phenoxy methyl penicillin (PO) 125mg for children younger than 3years;
A: phenoxy methyl penicillin (PO) 250mg for children 3 years and older, 12hourly until 5years of age in all children with SCA for prophylaxis against Pneumococcal Infection.

children with SCA for prophylaxis against Pneumococcal Infection.

blocks.text: Immunisation against pneumococcal infection
A: pneumococcal conjugate vaccine (PCV-13) from two months of age, 3 doses 8 weeks apart (i.e at age 2months, 4 months and 6 months), and a booster dose between 12-15 months.

runs.text: months and 6 months), and a booster dose between 12-15 months.

blocks.text: If the child has not previously received this vaccine, then at least one dose should be given between 6-18 years.
S: pneumococcal polysaccharide vaccine (PPSV-23) - at 2 years, then after every 5 years for life.

Disease Modifying Therapy
Principle of Dosage Initiation and Monitoring:
D: hydroxyurea (PO) 15 mg/kg/day 24hourly; (5–10 mg/kg/day if patient has chronic kidney disease).
OR
D: hydroxyurea (PO) 20mg/kg/day, starting dosage for infants and children.
Increase the dose by 2.5–5 mg/kg/day every 3 months. The maximum tolerated dose (MTD) should not exceed 30mg/kg/day.
If haematologic toxicity occurs;
Discontinue hydroxyurea until counts recover, usually 1-2 weeks,
Reinitiate hydroxyurea at a dose of 2.5mg/kg/day less than the dose given before onset of cytopenias to achieve the maximum tolerable therapeutic dose,
Do FBP according to the initiation schedule.
Note:
Clinical response to treatment with hydroxyurea may take 3-6months. A 6month trial on MTD is required before considering discontinuation due to treatment failure.

runs.text: before considering discontinuation due to treatment failure.

blocks.text: Hydroxyurea should be stopped at least three months prior to conception in both males and females
Hydroxyurea should be discontinued in all pregnant women
Hydroxyurea should be discontinued in all breastfeeding women
Chronic Transfusion Program
Regular scheduled blood transfusions, including both simple and exchange (manual or automated).
D: Chronic (Top-Up) Blood Transfusion:
Scheduled, long-term red cell transfusion program aims to prevent complications in SCD by maintaining the target Hb and reducing HbS level to 30%.

runs.text: Scheduled, long-term red cell transfusion program aims to prevent complications in SCD by maintaining the target Hb and reducing HbS level to 30%.

blocks.text: Potential risks include iron overload and alloimmunization; regular ferritin monitoring, chelation, and extended phenotype- matched, leukodepleted blood are essential.

runs.text: Potential risks include iron overload and alloimmunization; regular ferritin monitoring, chelation, and extended phenotype-

blocks.text: S: Exchange Blood Transfusion
Can be manual or automated by use of an Aphaeretic machine. Indicated in severe SCD patients with
Abnormal TCD
Cerebrovascular Accidents (CVAs)
Recurrent Acute Chest Syndrome (ACS) major surgery
Multi-organ failure, including Systemic Marrow Fat Embolism (SMFE)
Multiple pregnancies
Prevention of recurrent stroke.
SCD undergoing a Hematopoietic Stem Cell Transplant.
Relative Indications for Exchange Blood Transfusion
Intractable or very frequent severe crises
Major priapism unresponsive to other therapy.
Note:
Because the cardiovascular system adjusts to the chronic anaemia, blood transfusion is not routinely indicated in steady state SCD simply for the reason that haemoglobin level is below 8-10g/dl.

runs.text: in steady state SCD simply for the reason that haemoglobin level is below 8-10g/dl.

blocks.text: Packed red cell transfusion is preferred to minimize the risk of fluid overload.

SCD in pregnancy
Stop hydroxyurea 3 months before conception
Educate the patient about the risks associated with pregnancy in SCD.
Determine the haemoglobinopathy status of the partner.
Document pre-pregnancy baseline results, if any.
Refer the patient to a high-risk antenatal clinic for proper follow-up
Prescribe routine prenatal vitamins, see under Obstetrics and Gynaecology chapter
Prophylactic blood transfusion is not recommended.
Vaginal delivery is preferred unless there is an indication for cesarean section.
Prescribe prophylaxis for venous thromboembolism (VTE) for patients with additional risk factors for VTE e.g. history of VTE. See details under the coagulation disorders section 3.5

runs.text: history of VTE. See details under the coagulation disorders section 3.5

blocks.text: Monitor hydration status, warmth, and give analgesia as needed after delivery.
Assess and manage neonatal opioid dependency and withdrawal in all infants with a history of in utero opioid exposure.
Pharmacological Management.
A: acetylsalicylic acid (PO) 75mg 24hourly, starting from the second trimester to reduce the risk of pre-eclampsia.
Iron Overload in SCD
Excessive iron deposition in organs, including the liver, heart, pancreas, and endocrine glands, leading to fibrosis, organ dysfunction, and failure caused by Chronic Transfusions:

blocks.text: Each unit of transfused blood contains approximately 200–250 mg of iron and the body lacks a physiological mechanism to excrete excess iron.

Serum Ferritin
ALT, AST, GGT

Pharmacological Management
Iron Chelation:
C: deferiprone (PO) 25mg/kg 8hrly until serum ferritin falls to safe levels
OR
D: deferoxamine (IV/SC) 25-50mg/kg/day over 8-24 hours, 5 days per week

Check - Ferritin levels and LFTs 3 months, to monitor response, CBC weekly, stop if severe agranulocytosis develops. Continue if - patient remains transfusion dependent, ferritin still above 1000ng/Ml, in heavily transfused patients, and elevated MRI Liver/heart iron.

SCD Emergency Conditions:
Acute chest syndrome
Life-threatening – admit the patient in a high dependency unit or ICU,
Diagnostic criteria – respiratory distress (fast breathing, SPO2<95% on air) and/or pleuritic pain, cough, fever, tachycardia, infiltrates on CXR,
Investigations – arterial blood gases, creatinine, electrolytes, ALT, FBP, malaria test, blood and urine culture and sensitivity, CRP, CXR, HPLC,

runs.text: Investigations – arterial blood gases, creatinine, electrolytes,
ALT, FBP, malaria test, blood and urine culture and sensitivity, CRP, CXR, HPLC,

blocks.text: Management – Give supplemental oxygen to maintain SPO2>95%, analgesia for pain relief, fluids per hydration protocol, broad-spectrum antibiotics while awaiting culture and sensitivity results, top up blood transfusion or exchange transfusion if expertise available.

runs.text: Management – Give supplemental oxygen to maintain SPO2>95%, analgesia for pain relief, fluids per hydration protocol, broad-spectrum antibiotics while awaiting culture and sensitivity results, top up blood transfusion or exchange transfusion if expertise available.

blocks.text: Acute anaemia
Haemoglobin < 5g/dl or recent acute drop in Hb >2g/dl below steady state.
Causes – infection, splenic sequestration, haemolytic crisis and aplastic crisis.
Investigations – do FBP, reticulocyte count, creatinine, bilirubin, ALT, LDH, malaria test, urine and blood culture and sensitivity, blood grouping and cross-matching,

runs.text: and sensitivity, blood grouping and cross-matching,

blocks.text: Management – immediately transfuse packed red cells 10mls/kg over 4hours, repeat transfusion as needed as per transfusion protocol, treat the underlying cause, document the size of the liver and spleen.

runs.text: Management – immediately transfuse packed red cells 10mls/kg over 4hours, repeat transfusion as needed as per transfusion protocol, treat the underlying cause, document the size of the liver and spleen.
